Floetry was an English R&B duo comprising Marsha Ambrosius ("the Songstress") and Natalie Stewart ("the Floacist"). The group recorded two studio albums, one live album, and sold over 1,500,000 records worldwide. Formed in 1997, Floetry started on the performance poetry stage. They are two of the many artist responsible for developing the genre that is now known as Neo-Soul, while also popularizing the use of poetry and spoken word throughout music. In 2006 ladies parted ways to continue with their solo careers.
In 2015 Floetry reunited and performed their first show in nine years at Pepsi Funk Festival in College Park, Georgia. Despite announcing they would be recording a new album, Floetry subsequently split after the second leg of their reunion tour in August 2016.

Junior Senior were a Danish pop duo, active from 1998 to 2008. The duo consisted of [a=Jesper Mortensen] alias [a=Junior (11)] (vocals, guitar, bass guitar, keyboards) and [a=Jeppe Laursen] alias [a=Senior (2)] (vocals, keyboards, programming). Before forming Junior Senior 1998, Mortensen and Laursen had played together for one year during 1995-96 in [a=Ludox]. The name is explained by the simple fact that Laursen is the oldest and biggest of the two. The duo signed a deal with Danish label [l=Crunchy Frog] and released their debut album [m=108443] in 2002. It contained the single [m=40949], with vocals by [a=Thomas Troelsen] of [a=Superheroes], that became a massive radio hit in Denmark. [l=Universal] subsequently released both the album and the single internationally, and Move Your Feet gained worldwide success in 2003, most notably in the United Kingdom where it went straight to number 3 on the UK Singles Chart. The duo was invited to perform on Tops of the Pops as one of the few Danish acts ever. 2005 saw the release of second album [m=108447] that reached number 2 on the Japanese albums charts. Mortensen and Laursen announced that they would split and pursue solo projects on 26 September 2008.

Soul singer and songwriter.
Born February 10, 1937 in Black Mountain, North Carolina, USA.
Died February 24, 2025 in Manhattan, New York City, USA.
From 1969, she had recorded 16 albums, solo or in duet. She was produced through the years by [a=Joel Dorn], [a=Arif Mardin], [a=Ralph MacDonald], [a=Eugene McDaniels], [a=Joe Ferla], [a=Joseph Brooks], [a=Eric Mercury], [a=William Eaton], [a=William Salter], [a=Bob Crewe & Bob Gaudio], [a=Marcus Miller], [a=Michael Omartian], [a=Jerry Hey], [a=Andy Goldmark], [a=Barry Miles].
Best known for her hit singles "Killing Me Softly", "First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" and "Feel Like Makin' Love".
She duetted with [a=Donny Hathaway] and [a=Peabo Bryson], recording two albums with each one of them. In 1981, she recorded the soundtrack of "Bustin Loose" and sang the title song of the movie "Making Love" (1982), written by [a=Burt Bacharach]. A duet with  [a=Maxi Priest] entitled "Set The Night To Music" was released in 1991.  Her godson was jazz/funk keyboardist [a=Bernard Wright].

American soul/funk/jazz/disco band. 

Formed in 1975 in Los Angeles, California, USA, led by brothers [a=George Johnson] and [a=Louis Johnson]. Initially their line-up also included their cousin [a=Alex Weir]. 

They both started their careers as backing musicians of [a=Bobby Womack], [a=Billy Preston], et al., before later going it alone under the guidance of producer [a=Quincy Jones], who brought them to prominence using them on his own album "[m=101778]" (1975). 

They recorded eight albums between 1976 and 1988, and are most famous for their disco smash "[m=162779]" (1980), and their cover of the [a=Shuggie Otis] classic "[m=16857]" (1977).

[b]1996:[/b] Founded by Kevin Czinger after purchasing [l=Zoo Entertainment].

[b]Mid 1997:[/b] The "Zoo Entertainment" name ceases to be used.

[b]October 1997:[/b]  Czinger merges Volcano with [a=Dallas Austin]'s [l=Rowdy Records] to become [l=Freeworld Entertainment].

[b]March 1998:[/b] After being plagued with financial troubles as Freeworld, the label is purchased by the Zomba Label Group and subsequently renamed back Volcano Entertainment.

[b]December 2000:[/b] Volcano acquires the assets of [l=Capricorn Records] which had recently shut down following a reemergence in the early nineties.

[b]Volcano has reissued many of the releases originally found on [l=Zoo Entertainment], [l=Capricorn Records] and [l=Scotti Bros. Records].These releases should [i]not[/i] have release dates before 1996, and most likely were reissued later in the nineties.[/b]

North American reissues of [b]Zoo Entertainment[/b] releases vary from approximately [b]1998-2001[/b].
North American reissues of [b]Capricorn Records[/b] releases are almost all exclusively [b]2001[/b].
North American reissues of [b]Scotti Bros. Records[/b] releases are almost all exclusively [b]1998[/b].

Unofficial / counterfeit releases should use [l161583] instead.
